cohort: The study included 200 patients from a prenatal ward and labour room, divided into a control group (37-40 weeks gestational age) and a research group (more than 40 weeks gestational age).
finding: Postdated pregnancies were found to increase the rate of LSCS and instrumental deliveries.
mod_finding: The research found that postdated pregnancies increase LSCS and instrumental deliveries compared to term pregnancies.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over a 12-month period, comparing outcomes in patients presenting with different gestational ages at delivery.
gest_age: Control group: 37-40 weeks; Research group: > 40 weeks (majority 40-41 weeks)
